first.rationale: Competitor pricing pressure creates temptation to run promotional_pricing, but memory_73 explicitly warns that while it lifts SMB acquisition/revenue, it materially harms 30-day retention and should not be generalized as a strategy—this conflicts with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so it's excluded despite topical relevance. Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, and two independent durable memories (memory_31 signup simplification, memory_86 onboarding shortening) show consistent, non-conflicting evidence of durable activation/completion lifts for self-serve SMB accounts without noted retention harm. This directly targets a current metric decline with the most load-bearing and least risky prior evidence. I verify memory_73 to confirm the retention-harm caveat before ruling out pricing, and memory_31 to confirm the onboarding-adjacent evidence is as strong as summarized before committing the week's only experiment slot to it. Activation_messaging (memory_91) and enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) are plausible but address different funnel stages or segments not most urgently regressing; referral_incentive (memory_57) is a lower-urgency lever given no acute signal this week.

final.rationale: Verification confirms exp_73: promotional pricing yields strong short-term acquisition but -12% 30-day retention on the acquired cohort, explicitly flagged as unsustainable and not to be generalized — this rules it out given the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, despite competitive pressure making it tempting. Verification of exp_31 confirms signup simplification for SMB produced +9% activation, +4% qualified revenue, with only a marginal -1% retention effect (noted as within normal noise, not a flagged harm), and this is corroborated by the independent, consistent memory_86 (onboarding shortening improved completion and time-to-value). This convergence of two separate durable memories, one now source-verified with real numbers showing net-positive revenue and negligible retention cost, directly targets the two currently regressing metrics (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) with the strongest and least risky evidence base among all candidates. Running simplify_onboarding as a standard_experiment (not broad rollout) preserves appropriate uncertainty since exp_31 notes it 'holds on SMB; not replicated on other segments' — so scale is calibrated to that boundary rather than assuming universal applicability. This is the single best use of this week's one experiment slot.
